rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 'Performance and Error Analysis' and 'Application of New Methodology to Drip Irrigation Problem' (Figs. 2-8) report the authors' own numerical flow-model runs (1D Richards model; axisymmetric HYDRUS-2D) and their own training/testing of a self-organizing-map ANN that returns the water application time for a given initial soil moisture and desired wetted depth/radius.
rows.notes: The study develops and tests an ANN (SOM) that reproduces a numerical flow model and returns the trickle irrigation time needed to reach a target wetted soil volume. It reports only agreement between SOM output and the numerical model's test data (MSE, +/-1 cm deviation in Fig. 8) and CPU-time comparisons. It does not report any measured or modelled reduction in applied water, nor is any output compared with measurements from a real system (the HYDRUS-2D set-up is re-run from Meshkat et al. 1999; the lysimeter validation is Meshkat's, not the authors'). The 'improved irrigation efficiency' is asserted as an expected benefit, not demonstrated. Hence the study supports only a precondition (a tool to determine application time), not the claimed water-conservation effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 'Performance and Error Analysis' and 'Application of New Methodology to Drip Irrigation Problem' (Figs. 2-8) report the authors' own flow-model simulations and SOM training/testing to determine water application time for a desired saturated soil volume.
rows.notes: No crop, yield or biomass variable appears anywhere in the study; the only outputs are wetted depth/radius, application time and ANN error/CPU metrics compared against a numerical model (not against field or lab measurements by the authors). The reference to a 'crop-specific soil moisture profile' is a design target, not a measured production outcome. The study therefore supplies at most a precondition (determining application time to reach a target soil-moisture pattern) for the claimed yield-maximising effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 287-297). The paper is a methodological/simulation study: a SOM neural network trained on Richards-equation/HYDRUS-2D outputs to invert the irrigation-time problem for trickle irrigation. All validation is model-versus-model (SOM vs numerical solution); the only link to measurements is Meshkat et al.'s (1999) earlier lysimeter validation of HYDRUS-2D, which the authors cite and reproduce rather than test themselves. Neither water savings nor yield are quantified.
